title: Shoulder discomfort
overview: Shoulder pain has several possible causes; a physical examination may be needed.
generalCare: Keep gentle movement comfortable; reduce activities that worsen pain.
Keep comfortable movement within your current limits.
Get advice if symptoms persist, worsen or interfere with normal activities.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for worsening or persistent symptoms; sudden severe pain or inability to move needs urgent help.

title: Shoulder tendon irritation
overview: Tendon or bursa irritation can be associated with pain when using the shoulder. Location alone cannot establish the cause.
generalCare: Avoid strenuous exercises that aggravate symptoms.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek care if movement is very difficult or symptoms persist.

title: Pain around the outer elbow
overview: Outer elbow pain may occur with repeated gripping or wrist movements.
generalCare: Reduce activities that provoke symptoms.
Take breaks from repeated gripping or lifting that provokes pain.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment if pain persists despite reducing aggravating activity.

title: Tennis elbow
overview: Tennis elbow affects tendons near the outer elbow and can occur outside racket sports.
generalCare: Simple comfortable arm movements may help maintain motion.
Take breaks from repeated gripping or lifting that provokes pain.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment if symptoms persist after around two weeks of self-care.

title: Wrist discomfort
overview: Injury is one cause of wrist pain, but nerve and tendon problems can also contribute.
generalCare: Reduce painful tasks and heavy gripping.
Keep comfortable movement within your current limits.
Get advice if symptoms persist, worsen or interfere with normal activities.
whenToSeekHelp: Severe pain, shape changes or loss of feeling need prompt medical help.

title: Wrist sprain information
overview: A sprain can involve pain and swelling, but similar symptoms can occur with a fracture.
generalCare: Rest from aggravating activities while seeking advice if an injury is suspected.
whenToSeekHelp: Do not rely on self-care if you suspect a broken wrist.

title: Lower back discomfort
overview: Back pain is common and its cause is not always clear.
generalCare: Stay gently active as tolerated; avoid prolonged bed rest.
Change activities that clearly aggravate the pain.
Arrange an assessment for persistent or limiting symptoms.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek care if pain worsens or limits daily activities. New bladder or bowel changes with back pain require emergency help.

title: Back muscle strain information
overview: A pulled muscle can cause back pain, though other conditions can cause similar symptoms.
generalCare: Stop exercises that worsen symptoms and seek advice.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek emergency help for back pain after a serious accident or with new symptoms in both legs.

title: Knee discomfort
overview: Knee pain may follow twisting or overuse, but several joint conditions can cause similar discomfort.
generalCare: Reduce prolonged standing and painful loading.
Keep comfortable movement within your current limits.
Get advice if symptoms persist, worsen or interfere with normal activities.
whenToSeekHelp: Inability to bear weight, marked swelling or a hot joint with fever needs urgent assessment.

title: Knee tendon irritation
overview: Repeated jumping or running can be associated with pain between the kneecap and shin.
generalCare: Reduce aggravating loading while seeking appropriate advice.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for persistent pain, locking or giving way.

title: Ankle discomfort
overview: Ankle pain may follow exercise or footwear pressure; an injury may also need examination.
generalCare: Rest from aggravating activity and use comfortable footwear.
Keep comfortable movement within your current limits.
Get advice if symptoms persist, worsen or interfere with normal activities.
whenToSeekHelp: Severe pain, an abnormal shape or inability to walk needs urgent assessment.

title: Ankle sprain information
overview: Swelling and bruising after exercise can occur with a sprain. These symptoms do not exclude a fracture.
generalCare: Rest and elevate the ankle when comfortable.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek medical advice if pain worsens, recurs or interferes with normal activity.

title: Head discomfort and headaches
overview: Headaches can have several triggers, including stress and not drinking enough fluids. Selecting the head cannot identify the cause.
symptoms: A headache that recurs or changes with activity
generalCare: Drink water, eat regular meals and take breaks from prolonged screen use.
whenToSeekHelp: Get urgent advice for headaches triggered by exercise. Sudden extremely severe headache, new weakness, confusion, or a headache after a head injury needs emergency help.

title: Neck discomfort and stiffness
overview: Sleep position, posture and an injury can contribute to neck discomfort. Tingling or a cold arm needs medical assessment.
symptoms: Stiffness or discomfort when turning the head
generalCare: Keep movements gentle and comfortable. Avoid driving or cycling if limited neck movement makes it unsafe.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment if symptoms last several weeks, worry you, or come with tingling or a cold arm.

title: Chest discomfort: when to seek help
overview: Chest pain has many causes, including muscle strain, but location or exercise history cannot rule out a serious cause. Sudden persistent chest pain, spreading pain, or pain with breathlessness needs emergency help.
symptoms: Pain that may change with breathing or movement
generalCare: Get medical advice for unexplained chest pain rather than assuming it is exercise soreness.
whenToSeekHelp: Get emergency help for sudden pain that does not settle, pain spreading to the arms, neck, jaw or back, or chest pain with sweating, nausea, light-headedness or breathlessness.

title: Abdominal discomfort
overview: Abdominal pain can come from digestive and other conditions. It should not automatically be attributed to an abdominal workout.
symptoms: Bloating or changes in bowel habits
generalCare: Ask a pharmacist or clinician about suitable next steps for mild symptoms; seek assessment if pain persists or returns.
whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood, black sticky stools or difficulty breathing needs emergency help. Get urgent advice if pain rapidly worsens or occurs during pregnancy.

title: Upper back discomfort
overview: Back pain may involve muscle strain, but its cause is not always clear. Pain between the shoulders deserves medical assessment.
symptoms: Pain between or around the shoulder blades
generalCare: Continue gentle daily movement as tolerated and stop exercises that worsen symptoms.
Change activities that clearly aggravate the pain.
Arrange an assessment for persistent or limiting symptoms.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment for upper back pain, especially persistent or night pain. Chest pain, new symptoms in both legs, bladder or bowel changes, or a serious accident needs emergency help.

title: Upper arm discomfort
overview: Arm discomfort can have several causes. The place you feel pain does not establish whether a muscle, tendon or another structure is involved.
generalCare: Raise the arm if swollen; a heat or cold pack wrapped in a towel may ease discomfort.
whenToSeekHelp: Severe pain, difficulty moving, a change in shape or numbness needs prompt assessment. Sudden arm pain with chest pressure needs emergency help.

title: Forearm discomfort
overview: Pain in the lower arm can have several explanations and may need examination, especially after an injury.
symptoms: Aching or pain in the forearm
generalCare: A wrapped heat or cold pack may help discomfort; seek advice if symptoms persist.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek prompt assessment for severe pain, numbness or a change in shape. Arm pain with exercise that eases with rest needs urgent advice.

title: Hand and palm discomfort
overview: Hand pain can follow bruising or injury; tendon, joint and nerve problems may also cause symptoms. A location alone cannot distinguish them.
generalCare: Reduce activities that aggravate the pain and keep gentle hand movement comfortable.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek prompt help for severe pain, a change in shape or loss of feeling. Do not try to manage a suspected broken hand on your own.

title: Hip discomfort
overview: Hip pain may follow repetitive exercise or an injury, and joint conditions can also contribute. It may extend into the thigh.
symptoms: Pain around the hip or upper thigh
generalCare: Keep moving gently as tolerated while reducing painful loading.
whenToSeekHelp: Get emergency assessment for severe hip pain after an injury or inability to bear weight. A hot, swollen hip with fever needs urgent help.

title: Glute and buttock discomfort
overview: Pain in the buttock with burning, tingling or pain down one leg can occur with sciatica. Buttock location alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms: Buttock pain that may extend down a leg
generalCare: Keep gentle daily activity comfortable and avoid long periods of sitting or lying down.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for worsening or limiting symptoms. New numbness around the genitals or anus, bladder or bowel changes, or severe worsening symptoms in both legs needs emergency help.

title: Front thigh muscle discomfort
overview: A muscle strain can cause pain, tenderness and bruising after overstretching. Pain in the thigh can also have other causes.
generalCare: Protect a recent injury and pause the activity that aggravates it.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek urgent assessment for worsening pain, marked swelling or difficulty walking. Pain with one-sided leg swelling needs urgent advice; chest pain or breathlessness alongside it needs emergency help.

title: Hamstring discomfort
overview: The hamstrings run along the back of the thigh. A strain can happen during sport and may cause sudden pain, swelling or bruising.
symptoms: Pain or tenderness behind the thigh
Swelling, bruising or difficulty walking after injury
generalCare: Protect a recent injury, stop aggravating activity and elevate the leg when comfortable.
whenToSeekHelp: Get urgent assessment for severe or worsening pain, substantial swelling or bruising, or difficulty standing or walking.

title: Shin discomfort and exercise
overview: Shin splints can cause tenderness along the front of the lower leg after exercise. Other injuries can cause similar pain.
symptoms: Pain or tenderness along the shin
generalCare: Pause the exercise that provoked pain and consider comfortable lower-impact activity. Build exercise back up gradually.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment if pain is worsening or not improving. Severe pain after a shin injury needs urgent assessment.

title: Calf discomfort
overview: A calf muscle strain can follow overstretching, but calf pain must not automatically be treated as a sports injury. A blood clot can cause pain and swelling in one leg.
symptoms: Pain or tenderness in the calf
generalCare: Protect a suspected recent muscle injury and pause aggravating activity. Seek advice rather than exercising through unexplained swelling.
whenToSeekHelp: Get urgent medical advice for one-sided leg swelling and pain, especially with skin colour changes. Associated chest pain or breathlessness needs emergency help.

title: Foot discomfort
overview: Foot pain may follow exercise, pressure from footwear or an injury. A painful spot does not identify its cause.
symptoms: Pain on the top of the foot
generalCare: Rest from aggravating tasks and use comfortable, supportive footwear.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment if pain worsens, keeps returning, limits activity or comes with tingling. Severe injury pain, a change in shape or inability to walk needs urgent help.

title: Frozen shoulder
overview: Persistent pain with pronounced stiffness can occur when the shoulder capsule tightens. An examination is needed to distinguish it from tendon or joint problems.
symptoms: Difficulty reaching or turning the arm
generalCare: Keep movement gentle rather than forcing the joint.
Follow exercises chosen by a clinician or physiotherapist.
Avoid inventing strenuous gym exercises for a stiff, painful shoulder.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment for persistent stiffness or major movement restriction.

title: Swelling over the elbow tip
overview: An irritated bursa can cause a tender, swollen area over a joint. Examination may be needed to check for infection.
generalCare: Reduce pressure on the elbow.
A cold pack wrapped in a towel may help.
whenToSeekHelp: A hot swollen joint with fever, severe pain or inability to move needs urgent assessment.

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
overview: Pressure on the median nerve at the wrist can cause hand and finger symptoms, often worse at night. Other nerve problems can look similar.
symptoms: Symptoms that come and go, often at night
generalCare: Reduce repeated wrist bending and forceful gripping that provoke symptoms.
Ask a pharmacist or clinician whether a night wrist splint is suitable.
Seek assessment when symptoms persist or worsen.
whenToSeekHelp: New loss of feeling or marked weakness needs prompt assessment.

title: Trigger finger or thumb
overview: A finger tendon can catch as it moves, leaving the finger bent or producing a click when it straightens. A clinician can assess persistent catching.
symptoms: Clicking, catching or locking of a finger
Stiffness or pain near the finger base
generalCare: Reduce the repetitive gripping that aggravates it.
Discuss persistent symptoms and possible splinting with a clinician.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment if the finger remains stuck or normal activities are affected.

title: Meniscus injury information
overview: The meniscus cushions the knee. A twist can damage it, but pain, clicking or swelling alone cannot confirm a tear.
symptoms: Catching, giving way or difficulty straightening
generalCare: Pause twisting and impact activities that aggravate pain.
Keep comfortable movement without forcing a locked knee.
Seek an assessment to guide the next steps.
whenToSeekHelp: Inability to bear weight, a locked knee or marked swelling needs prompt medical assessment.

title: Pain around the kneecap
overview: Patellofemoral pain describes discomfort around or behind the kneecap. Activity, training load and how the joint moves may contribute; a physical assessment helps identify the cause.
symptoms: An ache at the front of the knee
Pain with stairs, squatting or running
Discomfort after prolonged sitting with the knee bent
generalCare: Reduce the activity that provokes symptoms.
Choose comfortable lower-impact activity while seeking advice.
A clinician or physiotherapist can assess movement and appropriate exercises.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment for persistent pain; major swelling or inability to walk needs urgent advice.

title: Heel and arch pain
overview: Plantar fasciitis involves the tissue along the sole. Pain near the heel or arch may be worse with the first steps after rest; other foot conditions can cause similar pain.
symptoms: Pain under the heel or along the arch
Pain on first standing after sleep or sitting
generalCare: Use comfortable shoes with heel cushioning and arch support.
Reduce long periods of standing and painful impact exercise.
Ask a clinician about appropriate stretches if symptoms continue.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for worsening pain, tingling, or symptoms limiting daily activity.

title: Pain in the ball of the foot
overview: Pain under the forefoot is called metatarsalgia. Footwear pressure, exercise and several other conditions may contribute.
symptoms: Aching or burning beneath the forefoot
generalCare: Reduce aggravating walking or running.
Try comfortable footwear with room for the toes.
Ask a pharmacist or clinician about suitable cushioning.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment if pain recurs, worsens, affects walking or comes with reduced sensation.

title: Tension-type headache information
overview: A pressing or tightening headache on both sides can occur with tension-type headaches. The pattern is a starting point for discussion, not confirmation of a cause.
symptoms: Pressure or tightness on both sides
Tenderness around the head or neck
generalCare: Try relaxation and regular sleep habits.
Notice whether stress or caffeine relates to recurring headaches.
Keep a record to discuss with a clinician.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for frequent or severe headaches, and urgent help for a new warning sign.

title: Migraine information
overview: Migraine can involve a throbbing headache with nausea or sensitivity to light and sound. Some people notice an aura. New neurological symptoms should not be assumed to be migraine.
symptoms: Throbbing pain, often on one side
generalCare: A quiet, dark room may be more comfortable during an episode.
Keep regular meals and sleep habits.
Discuss frequent or changing headaches with a clinician.
whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe headache, new weakness, confusion or loss of vision needs emergency help.

title: Chest-wall inflammation information
overview: Costochondritis affects the rib connections at the breastbone. It may cause sharp pain with movement, pressure or deep breathing. Those features do not rule out heart or lung problems.
symptoms: Discomfort with upper-body movement or deep breathing
generalCare: Get medical advice for unexplained chest pain.
If a clinician has confirmed a chest-wall cause, discuss suitable activity changes and pain relief.
whenToSeekHelp: Persistent sudden chest pain, spreading pain or pain with breathlessness needs emergency help.

title: Indigestion-related symptoms
overview: Indigestion may cause fullness, bloating or heartburn after eating. Abdominal pain has many other causes and should not automatically be labelled indigestion.
generalCare: Notice food and drink triggers.
Avoid eating close to bedtime if it provokes symptoms.
Ask a pharmacist about suitable options for mild symptoms.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek assessment for persistent symptoms, swallowing difficulty, unexplained weight loss or bleeding.

title: Biceps tendon irritation
overview: The biceps tendon near the shoulder can become irritated. Discomfort may travel down the upper arm and overlap with other shoulder problems.
symptoms: Pain near the front of the shoulder or upper arm
Pain with overhead lifting or reaching backward
generalCare: Reduce painful overhead lifting.
Avoid repeatedly testing the painful movement.
Seek assessment for persistent pain or weakness before resuming strenuous loads.
whenToSeekHelp: A sudden injury with significant weakness or loss of movement needs prompt assessment.

title: Neck-related nerve symptoms
overview: Irritation of a nerve in the neck can cause pain travelling down an arm. Similar symptoms can arise elsewhere, so examination may be needed.
symptoms: Pain travelling from neck to arm
Weakness in an arm or hand
generalCare: Reduce positions that aggravate symptoms.
Avoid forceful neck movements or self-testing.
Arrange a clinical assessment for ongoing arm symptoms.
whenToSeekHelp: New or worsening weakness or loss of sensation needs prompt assessment.

title: Achilles tendon discomfort
overview: The Achilles tendon connects the calf to the heel. Repeated loading can contribute to irritation; location alone cannot distinguish this from a tear or another injury.
symptoms: Stiffness at the back of the heel, especially in the morning
Tenderness or swelling along the tendon
generalCare: Reduce painful running and jumping.
Avoid repeatedly loading the painful tendon to test it.
Seek guidance on gradual loading and suitable footwear.
whenToSeekHelp: A sudden pop with difficulty walking or pushing off needs prompt assessment.

title: Focal shin pain and bone stress
overview: Repeated loading can cause a bone stress injury. Pain in a specific spot after increased training deserves assessment rather than assuming it is shin splints.
symptoms: Pain with loading that may later occur at rest
generalCare: Stop impact activity that provokes the pain.
Arrange assessment before resuming running or jumping.
Discuss recent training changes with a clinician.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek prompt assessment for worsening pain, pain at rest or difficulty bearing weight.

title: Quadriceps strain information
overview: A strain can affect the muscles at the front of the thigh after a forceful movement.
generalCare: Pause painful sporting activity.
Protect a recent injury and seek advice if function is affected.
whenToSeekHelp: Marked weakness, substantial swelling or difficulty walking needs assessment.

title: Hamstring strain and activity
overview: A forceful movement can strain the muscles behind the thigh. Severity cannot be judged from the pain location alone.
generalCare: Stop the activity that caused the pain.
Return to demanding sport with appropriate professional guidance.
whenToSeekHelp: A pop with marked pain, weakness or difficulty walking needs prompt assessment.

title: Outer hip and gluteal tendon discomfort
overview: Gluteal tendinopathy can cause pain over the outer hip, where gluteal tendons attach. It differs from buttock pain travelling down the leg, but symptoms may overlap.
symptoms: Pain with stairs or standing on one leg
generalCare: Reduce positions that compress the painful outer hip.
Avoid repeatedly lying on the painful side.
A physiotherapist can assess suitable load changes and exercises.
whenToSeekHelp: Arrange assessment for persistent or limiting symptoms; sudden severe pain after injury needs urgent advice.

title: Bursa irritation around the hip
overview: An irritated bursa can cause an achy, tender area around a joint. Other hip problems can feel similar.
generalCare: Reduce direct pressure on the painful area.
A wrapped cold pack may ease discomfort.
whenToSeekHelp: Fever with a hot, swollen joint or severe movement difficulty needs urgent help.

title: Muscular upper back discomfort
overview: A muscle strain is one possible explanation for discomfort after a forceful or repetitive activity. Upper back pain still deserves assessment if it persists or worries you.
generalCare: Reduce aggravating loading.
Discuss persistent pain and appropriate movement with a clinician.
whenToSeekHelp: Seek urgent help for rapidly worsening pain or back pain with chest symptoms.

title: Calf muscle strain information
overview: A sudden push-off or overstretch can strain a calf muscle. Unexplained one-sided swelling must not be assumed to be a strain.
generalCare: Stop painful running or jumping.
Protect a recent injury and arrange assessment if walking is affected.
whenToSeekHelp: New one-sided leg swelling needs urgent advice. Chest pain or breathlessness alongside it needs emergency help.

title: Back-related leg pain information
overview: Sciatica can cause burning or sharp pain through the buttock and down one leg. A clinician may need to distinguish it from muscle, joint or other nerve problems.
generalCare: Continue comfortable everyday movement.
Avoid long periods of sitting or lying still.
Arrange assessment if symptoms persist, worsen or limit daily activity.
whenToSeekHelp: New bladder or bowel changes, groin numbness or severe symptoms in both legs needs emergency help.

title: Exercise-related chest muscle discomfort
overview: Chest muscles can be strained during exercise. Pain that follows exercise or changes with movement cannot safely identify a muscle strain by itself.
symptoms: Pain following chest exercise or an injury
generalCare: Get medical advice for unexplained chest pain.
Discuss exercise changes after the cause has been assessed.
whenToSeekHelp: Sudden persistent pain, spreading pain, sweating or breathlessness needs emergency help.
